# Editorial graphics

Thin lines and flat shapes that make an abstract idea visible: scale as rings, growth as a stack, attention as rays, a share as a bar. Built on `editorial-kit` (cite both).

## Rings and orbits

```html
<svg class="ed-lines" width="1080" height="1350">
  <g id="c-orbits" data-ed-rings="540 900 110 64 6 0.34" data-ed-class="ed-thin"></g>   <!-- cx cy r0 step n ratio -->
</svg>
<div class="ed-pos ed-label ed-in" id="c-m1" style="left:600px; top:860px">10</div>  <!-- markers on the rings -->
```
```js
E.draw(tl, R.querySelectorAll("#c-orbits path"), 0.6, { duration: 1.1, stagger: 0.12 });
E.pop(tl, R.querySelectorAll(".c-marker"), 1.4, { stagger: 0.08 });
```

- Rings = levels, reach, scale ("10 → 110"); a small cut-out at the centre is what everything orbits. Ratio 0.3–0.4 tilts them into orbits (a plane seen in perspective).
- Draw from the inside out; markers (`ed-label` numbers on small `ed-dot`s) pop on as each ring is named.

## Rays

`<path class="ed-thin" data-ed-path="rays 540 520 300 460 40"/>` — attention, energy, an idea radiating. Pop the rays (`E.pop`, scale 0.8 → 1) or draw them with a stagger; put the subject in the middle (a halo, like the arch portrait).

## Stacks, waves

- `stack x y w n gap` — a pile of coins (money, accumulation). Two stacks side by side, one tall (the accent) and one short (ink), each with its number: the comparison IS the explanation. Reveal with `E.grow(… {from:"bottom"})` on a wrapper.
- `wave x y w amp periods` — a signal, a heartbeat, a market. Draw left to right.

## The big number

```html
<div class="ed-pos ed-display ed-in" id="c-num" style="left:560px; top:620px; font-size:190px; color:var(--ed-field)">0%</div>
<div class="ed-pos ed-label ed-in" id="c-num-l" style="left:566px; top:820px">qualified leads</div>
```
```js
E.rise(tl, $("c-num"), 1.0, { distance: 40 });
E.count(tl, $("c-num"), 1.0, { to: 829, suffix: "%", duration: 1.4 });
E.rise(tl, $("c-num-l"), 1.6, { distance: 20 });
```

- A number is only as clear as its comparison: always give the reference ("829% vs 160%", "1 in 3", "twice as long as …").
- Round it for a newcomer (`829%` → "8×" when the brief allows); keep the exact figure only if the brief insists. Every number traces to the brief or the product facts; otherwise a placeholder `[X]`.
- Thin rules lead the eye from the number to what it measures (`line` paths, drawn).

## Simple charts

```html
<div class="ed-grid"></div>
<div class="ed-bar ed-in" id="c-b1" style="left:200px; top:520px; width:120px; height:480px; background:var(--ed-ink)"></div>
<div class="ed-bar ed-in" id="c-b2" style="left:380px; top:280px; width:120px; height:720px"></div>
```
```js
E.grow(tl, [$("c-b1"), $("c-b2")], 0.8, { from: "bottom", duration: 0.9, stagger: 0.25 });
E.highlight(tl, $("c-hl"), 2.2, 0.5);                // the one category that matters
```

- Two to five bars, no axis clutter: a baseline rule, a mono label under each, the value on top. One bar in the field colour (the point), the rest ink or muted.
- A source line in `ed-label` at the bottom when the brief gives one ("Source: …"); never invent a source.

## Critical constraints

- Thin lines (2–4 px), round caps; one stroke colour per frame plus ink.
- Line-art in unscaled svgs; generated by `data-ed-path` / `data-ed-rings`, never hand-typed long `d` strings.
- Numbers and labels are real text (HTML), never baked into pictures.
